argumentMap.attributedThesis: AIDB argues that agents are moving from private, one-person workflows into shared team spaces where colleagues can see, steer and continue the same work.
reasoningChain: Most consequential knowledge work depends on team context rather than one person's private chat.
A private agent repeatedly loses shared history and makes collaboration harder to inspect.
Shared sessions, permissions and a maintained context repository can turn the agent into a team work surface.
Teams should choose one bounded workflow, score it for repeatability and risk, and learn before expanding.
argumentMap.editorialBoundary: This is AIDB's analysis and programme framing, not an independently established market law. Product facts and metrics require their original sources.

items.heading: Agents have only been able to impact half of work
items.reason: Useful framing, but the quantitative premise still needs the exact surveys and should not become a standalone claim.

items.heading: Four free programs this year — every one of them individual
items.reason: Programme history and promotion do not create a distinct reader job.

items.heading: There are still no AI experts — just people who have practiced more
items.reason: A practical encouragement frame, but it is an attributed generalisation rather than a factual finding.

items.heading: The majority of knowledge work runs through team context
items.reason: The cited survey claims require exact primary recovery before publication.

items.heading: Every early agent experiment served an audience of one
items.reason: Interpretive history that supports the episode thesis but is too broad as a factual headline.

items.heading: Managing a fleet of agents is now part of being a knowledge worker
items.reason: Potential teaching direction, but 'table stakes' overstates current practice for many readers and workplaces.

items.heading: The next frontier of agent design is the shared spaces teams inhabit
items.route: Concept of the Week / AI Fundamentals
items.reason: A useful concept bridge from individual prompts to shared context, permissions and continuity.

items.heading: Multiplayer AI, defined in four shifts
items.reason: The four shifts provide a usable explanation if translated into ordinary language and tied to current products.

items.heading: Every tried mirror agents — then moved them into shared spaces
items.reason: The exact Every account must be read and its limits retained before reuse.

items.heading: Claude Tag is the clearest product expression of multiplayer AI so far
items.reason: Claude Tag is verified product context, but the superlative is AIDB's judgment and the June launch is not fresh news.

items.heading: A shared agent means nobody explains things from scratch twice
items.reason: Reader-useful benefit when paired with staleness, permission and ownership caveats.

items.heading: 65% of Anthropic's product team code comes from a shared agent
items.reason: Anthropic states this as an internal vendor metric; it is not independent evidence of typical team outcomes.

items.heading: OpenClaw's rebuild forced multiplayer on its own maintainers
items.reason: LAiDIES already published the shared-session development; retain only distinct supporting context.

items.heading: The session becomes a shared piece of work
items.reason: This is the same underlying product change, not a new event.

items.heading: Y Combinator's fall 2026 request for startups: multiplayer AI
items.reason: Verified as an investor thesis, not proof that the market direction is settled.

items.heading: AI has not had its multiplayer moment yet
items.reason: Useful attributed thesis for tracking, not a factual conclusion.

items.heading: Anywhere a team crowds around one problem, there should be a shared agent
items.reason: Overly broad recommendation that ignores risk, privacy, permissions and whether the work is repeatable.

items.heading: The Multiplayer AI Sprint
items.reason: Do not recommend the programme until current access, privacy and reader fit are checked; its promotion is not news.

items.heading: Sprint session one: find out what your team is actually running
items.route: Paige / Behind the Build / internal practice
items.reason: A bounded inventory is useful before a team centralises tools or context.

items.heading: Inventory barriers or borrow a power user
items.reason: Useful adoption idea when framed as a limited experiment, not generic career advice.

items.heading: Sprint session two: build the shared context repository
items.reason: Directly connects current agent practice to maintained teaching about context, memory and projects.

items.heading: Score shared-agent candidates on four axes
items.reason: A practical selection tool, subject to a current-practice review and explicit security axis.

items.heading: Sprint session four: ship one shared agent and repeat
items.reason: A small pilot with observable results is preferable to organisation-wide adoption by assertion.

items.heading: Squint at it and the direction is obvious
items.reason: AIDB's conclusion is worth tracking but does not itself establish inevitability.

primaryChecks.note: Anthropic's June 23 product announcement supports the shared-channel, permissions and ambient-agent description; internal 65% metric remains a vendor claim.
Release documentation supports shared-session controls; the development is already covered by LAiDIES.
YC presents multiplayer AI as a Fall 2026 request-for-startups thesis, not independent evidence of adoption.
Exact article identified; any organisational-outcome claims require full source review before reuse.

audienceGap.readerQuestion: When does sharing an AI workspace reduce repeated explanation, and when does it create stale-context, access or accountability problems?
audienceGap.plainLanguageRule: Start with the familiar problem of teammates repeating background in separate chats, then explain the shared workspace, who can see or steer it, and who owns corrections.

bigPictureThemeReview.reason: This adds team ownership and permissions to the existing responsibility and shared-infrastructure question. It does not yet earn a separate Big Picture draft.

internalPracticeReview.reason: LAiDIES already uses durable shared files and multiple agents. Pilot shared context only for repeated collaborative work, with explicit ownership, freshness and access checks; no framework mutation follows automatically.
